data.name: MediaWiki Action API - GET (read-only / discovery)
data.description:
Overview:
The MediaWiki Action API is a single HTTP endpoint (api.php) that exposes many actions (modules) via query parameters. Use GET for read-only requests such as action=query, action=parse, action=opensearch, action=help and other informational/listing modules.
Documentation: https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Action_API and https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Special:ApiHelp
Quick Start:
- Base URL: {{baseUrl}}/w/api.php
- Minimum: set action={{action}} and format={{format}} as query parameters.
- Example quick call: GET {{baseUrl}}/w/api.php?action=parse&format=json&page=Pet_door
Parameters Explained:
- action (required): The name of the action/module to invoke (e.g. query, parse, opensearch, help). See the documentation for allowed action names. Use {{action}}.
- format (optional): Response format. Typical: json. Use {{format}} (default jsonfm on some wikis, but json is recommended).
- formatversion (optional): Format version for JSON output (1 or 2). Use {{formatVersion}}.
- maxlag (optional): Integer. Max DB replication lag allowed before returning maxlag error. Use {{maxlag}}.
- smaxage / maxage (optional): Integers for HTTP cache headers. {{smaxage}}, {{maxage}}.
- origin (optional): Required for cross-origin AJAX (CORS). Use {{origin}} (must be in URL for preflight requests).
- assert / assertuser (optional): Enforce that the requester is logged in/anon/bot or a named user. {{assert}} / {{assertUser}}.
- requestid (optional): Echoed in response for tracing. {{requestId}}.
- servedby, curtimestamp, responselanginfo (optional): Diagnostic flags. {{servedBy}}, {{curTimestamp}}, {{responseLangInfo}}.
- Common module-specific parameters (examples):
  - page / titles / pageid: identify pages. {{page}}, {{titles}}, {{pageId}}.
  - prop / list / meta / generator: query submodule selectors. {{prop}}, {{list}}, {{meta}}, {{generator}}.
  - rvlimit, limit, offset, continue (pagination): {{limit}}, {{offset}}, {{continue}}.
  - search (opensearch/search modules): {{search}}.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- maxlag (API error object): Set maxlag to a lower value or retry later; or remove intensive parameters.
- badtoken / notloggedin (when asserting or performing modifying actions via GET): Use POST and obtain a proper token via the tokens API first.
- 400 BadRequest (HTTP): Malformed parameter combinations; ensure action and format are present and valid values.
- 403 Forbidden (HTTP) or API error: Missing required permissions for the requested action; authenticate or request proper rights.
- 409 Conflict (API-level for edits): Use basetimestamp/starttimestamp for edit conflict resolution.
Edge Cases:
- Many write operations (login/edit/upload/delete) are disallowed via GET for security (tokens must be supplied and the request is expected via POST). Use the POST request variant for those.
- Some wikis disable or extend modules; available modules may differ between wikis.
- CORS preflight requires origin in the request URL (not the POST body).
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Rate limits/quota are wiki-dependent. Wikimedia sites apply throttling and abuse filters. Obey etiquette, back off on 429-like responses and respect maxlag.
Documentation:
- Canonical overview: https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Action_API
- Local autogenerated help (per-wiki): https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Special:ApiHelp
data.evaluateGuide:
Reads Wiktionary data and metadata through MediaWiki modules, including queries, parsing, search, help, and listings. Use it for read-only discovery and informational responses.
Use for: query pages, parse wikitext, search terms, inspect API help
Not supported: creating or editing pages, deleting content, administrative actions

data.name: Read a batch of leads by internal ID, or unique property values
data.evaluateGuide:
Reads multiple HubSpot lead records in one operation using internal IDs or unique property values. Use it to retrieve selected lead data efficiently.
Use for: batch-read leads, retrieve leads by ID, look up leads by unique value
Not supported: creating leads, updating records, deleting records
